items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-07-23, 08-03
items.q: Now Harry Shields was a clarinet player on the band and couldn't read.

ctx.x: Well, how did you work the arrangements out? You said, somewhere had?

Well, some more head arrangements. Joe Rodas, uh, was an absolutely wonderful musician. And could write for strings, could write for any combination you wanted. And he did most of the writing. Uh, the dance book was Joe's. stuff had that knack I can remember, we were working at the club slipper at the little bar next door to it which later became the dream bar that you're probably familiar with. They had a piano player in there and the Dukes of Dixieland were doing some syndicated, 15 minute syndicated television…

Yeah, well, he's one of those people that I heard people talk about. And of course, I always thought of him as a comedian, a clown, who flew around with the trombone and play stuff. And so often I heard him do, he was very, very funny. I'm not belittling him.
